key_insight: VideoAtlas encodes long videos as a hierarchical, lossless, navigable grid that provides an at-a-glance overview and enables model access to fine-grained regions with logarithmic compute, avoiding captioning or lossy summarization.
problem_solved: Addresses two core barriers to extending language models to video: (1) lossy representations that collapse visual fidelity, and (2) inability to scale to long-context video without heavy preprocessing or collapsing to text.
method: Hierarchical grid representation: organize video into multi-resolution spatial–temporal tiles so the whole video and details coexist.
Navigable, lossless access: allow random-access zooming into tiles so models can attend to relevant regions without scanning everything.
Logarithmic compute scaling and task-agnostic design: retrieval/navigation cost grows sublinearly with video length and requires no captioning or bespoke preprocessing.
impact: Makes long-form video tractable for multimodal models while preserving pixel-level fidelity, reducing preprocessing overhead and compute for tasks like retrieval, QA, summarization, and interactive agents. Enables scalable, general-purpose video reasoning at lengths previously infeasible.
